sentences.text: Ponerosteus is a dubious genus containing only one known species, Ponerosteus exogyrarum.
The name translates to "bad" or "useless bone," reflecting the poor condition of the fossil.
The holotype, a cast of a tibia found near Holubice, was first named Iguanodon exogirarum by Antonín Frič in 1878.
Frič later renamed the specimen Procerosaurus in 1905, not realizing the name was already taken.
The holotype is apparently the inner surface of a tibia belonging to an animal that may or may not be a dinosaur.
The holotype fossil is currently displayed at the National Museum in Prague.
Ponerosteus is now classified within Archosauromorpha rather than as a dinosaur and falls within the class Ornithischia.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Ponerosteus as Ornithopoda.
The animal lived approximately 96 million years ago during the Cenomanian stage of the Cretaceous in the Korycanar Formation of the Czech Republic.
